verdict.tagline: Fast fights marred by matchmaking gaps and heavy network lag.
for_you_if: you want a fighting game that runs smoothly on older hardware
not_for_you_if: you encounter severe input delay and server lag
you struggle against mismatched opponents and move spam
you want to unlock the full character roster without spending money

distortion_flags.sentence: Sentiment rises initially before dropping sharply among long-term players.
Recent reviews skew significantly more negative than the historical lifetime average.

cohorts.label: <2h refund window
cohorts.summary: Beginners face steep barriers against experienced players using complex combos and repetitive moves.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe struggling against experienced opponents in unranked matches who use repetitive moves or advanced combos that are difficult for beginners to counter.

citations.review_text:
I really wanted to like this game. I saw it, thought it looked fun, and decided to give it a try. After an hour and a few games, though, I'm already done.

Trying to play unranked as a complete beginner is absolutely miserable. I'm constantly getting destroyed by people who either spam the same moves over and over or pull off perfectly calculated combos that I have absolutely no idea how to counter. I don't mind losing, I expect to lose when I'm new to a game, but there's a huge difference between losing and feeling like you aren't even allowed to play the game.

How are you supposed to actually learn and improve when your first experience is getting matched against players who clearly know the game inside and out? There needs to be some kind of proper beginner experience or skill-based matchmaking so new players can actually learn the mechanics, experiment with characters, and slowly improve without getting completely stomped every match.

Maybe the ranked system is better for this, but why should I have to suffer through unranked matches just to reach a point where the game might actually become enjoyable?

The game seemed fun, but I don't even get the chance to properly get into it. It's incredibly frustrating, and honestly, as a new player, I can't recommend it.
Played this game for about an hour. Got comboed into oblivion 0.1/10 dont recommend. If you want to go through a couple desks, mice, and keyboards this game is for you.

This game is... an interesting experience. One moment you are playing with your friends, and you are laughing your but off because they are in a rage because you are denying them their weapons with Ruptues side sigs, and then the next moment you are playing against a sigging Loki, and you are the one who is crashing out. But overall it can be fun, especially if you do find one of the few respectable players that you actually have fun fighting with. I would not particularly suggest playing online if you value your sanity, but if you are playing it with your friends or family as a couch party game, it's great. 

8.5/10 as a couch party game
